DRAM caches have shown excellent potential in capturing the spatial and temporal data locality of applications capitalizing on advances of 3D-stacking technology; however, they are still far from their ideal performance. Besides the unavoidable DRAM access to fetch the requested data, tag access is in the critical path, adding significant latency and energy costs. Existing approaches are not able to remove these overheads and in some cases limit DRAM cache design options. For instance, caching DRAM cache tags adds constant latency to every access; accessing the DRAM cache using the TLB calls for OS support and DRAM cachelines as large as a page; reusing the last-level cache (LLC) tags to access the DRAM cache limits LLC performance as it requires indexing the LLC using higher-order address bits. In this article, we introduce
            Decoupled Fused Cache
            , a DRAM cache design that alleviates the cost of tag accesses by fusing DRAM cache tags with the tags of the on-chip LLC without affecting LLC performance. In essence, the
            Decoupled Fused Cache
            relies in most cases on the LLC tag access to retrieve the required information for accessing the DRAM cache while avoiding additional overheads. Compared to current DRAM cache designs of the same cacheline size,
            Decoupled Fused Cache
            improves system performance by 6% on average and by 16% to 18% for large cacheline sizes. Finally,
            Decoupled Fused Cache
            reduces DRAM cache traffic by 18% and DRAM cache energy consumption by 7%.

result.paraphrase: DRAM caches have demonstrated strong potential for capturing applications’ spatial and temporal locality, thanks to advances in 3D-stacking technology, but their performance remains well below ideal. In addition to the unavoidable DRAM access needed to retrieve requested data, tag lookup lies on the critical path and introduces substantial latency and energy overhead. Existing methods cannot eliminate these costs and sometimes constrain DRAM cache design choices. For example, storing DRAM cache tags in DRAM adds a fixed latency to every access; using the TLB to access the DRAM cache requires OS support and cachelines as large as a page; and reusing LLC tags to reach the DRAM cache reduces LLC performance because it forces the LLC to be indexed with higher-order address bits. This article introduces Decoupled Fused Cache, a DRAM cache design that cuts the cost of tag accesses by combining DRAM cache tags with on-chip LLC tags without harming LLC performance. In most cases, Decoupled Fused Cache depends on the LLC tag access to obtain the information needed for DRAM cache access while avoiding extra overhead. Relative to existing DRAM cache designs with the same cacheline size, it improves system performance by 6% on average and by 16% to 18% for large cacheline sizes. It also lowers DRAM cache traffic by 18% and DRAM cache energy use by 7%.
